page: Vultr vbm-8c-132gb-v2 is a dedicated bare metal server belonging to the Bare Metal NVMe family. It features an Intel Xeon 2388G processor built on the x86_64 architecture, operating at a base clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The system provides 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs via hyperthreading, backed by a 16 MB L3 cache. Memory resources consist of 128.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, translating to 8.0 GB of memory per physical core. Local storage is comprised of a 3840 GB NVMe SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present.

Benchmark results indicate a mix of average and top-tier capabilities. The single-core and multi-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng, falls within the average range, as does the PassMark CPU score of 23,271.22. However, single-threaded gzip compression achieves top-tier performance at 36.27 GB/sec, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression is strong at 14.14 GB/sec. The PassMark memory score is also in the top tier. Conversely, uncached large-block memory bandwidth is weak, with read speeds at 36.93 GB/sec and write speeds at 19.38 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this bare metal configuration offers high resource density with dedicated CPU allocation and substantial NVMe storage, bypassing virtualization overhead. The tradeoff lies in the memory subsystem, where cached small-block reads are fast, but uncached large-block operations show reduced throughput. This hardware profile is suited for database operations, static web serving, and lightweight text-generation tasks, as evidenced by its average Redis SET throughput and stable medium-model LLM inference speeds.
